goal: 3d print a model from a design
summary: Go from an idea to a printed physical object: author or repair a 3D model, slice it into printer G-code, run open firmware on the printer, and drive the job from a print host. Every stage is a real, existing open-source project; the only thing to buy is the printer.

capabilities.query: cadquery parametric cad python model stl

build_steps.title: Author or import the model
build_steps.detail: Script the part in CadQuery (or OpenSCAD) and export STL, or start from a downloaded STL.

build_steps.title: Repair the mesh
build_steps.detail: Run trimesh to confirm the mesh is watertight and fix normals/holes before slicing. A non-manifold mesh slices into garbage.

build_steps.title: Slice to G-code
build_steps.detail: Open the STL in PrusaSlicer/OrcaSlicer, pick your printer + filament profile, set layer height and infill, and export G-code.

build_steps.title: Flash firmware (if building/upgrading the printer)
build_steps.detail: A commercial printer ships with firmware. For a hackable/upgraded printer, flash Marlin (on-board) or move motion planning to a Pi with Klipper.

build_steps.title: Run the job from a host
build_steps.detail: Upload the G-code to OctoPrint (or Mainsail for Klipper), level the bed, and print. Watch the first layer.

safety: FDM hot ends reach 200-300C and heated beds 60-110C. Don't leave prints unattended long-term without a smoke/thermal cutoff, ventilate when printing ABS/ASA, and keep hands clear of the moving gantry.
